steps.text: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 runs on Highball's native arm64 engine, which translates its DirectX 12 through vkd3d-proton and MoltenVK. The game asks for Shader Model 6.7, which this route reports. Steam has to be online, because the game signs in to its servers through Steam. The first start asks for your Microsoft account inside the game, and later starts remember it. The first start takes about nine minutes to reach the start screen while the game activates its packages and compiles its shaders, and every later start about six, since the engine keeps the compiled shaders for the game. The loading screen plays its videos and shows the progress the whole way. The game is told it has three eighths of this Mac's memory as video memory (12 GB on a 32 GB Mac). The Steam overlay is off, as in every flight measured so far. For a smooth flight set the upscaler in the game (Settings, General, Graphics): Anti-aliasing to AMD FSR 3.1 and AMD FSR to Balanced. On a base M4 at 1080p that gives 26 fps parked and 25 on the take-off roll at the Medium preset against 18 and 16 with TAA, with a steadier frame time, and the picture stays clean; the Low-End preset with the same upscaler reaches 30, and FSR Quality keeps more detail at 24. Motion blur is best off on a Mac (Settings, General, Graphics, Global Rendering Quality, Motion Blur): at the frame rates a Mac reaches it smears the whole picture when the view turns and leaves stepped trails behind the ground at takeoff.

knownIssues.symptom: Around 18 frames a second at the Medium preset, with uneven frame times
knownIssues.cause: the game renders every pixel at full resolution through vkd3d-proton and MoltenVK, and a base M4 has no headroom for that
knownIssues.fix: Settings, General, Graphics: Anti-aliasing set to AMD FSR 3.1 and AMD FSR to Balanced, then ESC to save (26 fps parked on a base M4 at Medium, 30 at the Low-End preset; Quality keeps more detail at 24)

knownIssues.symptom: The start screen takes about nine minutes to come the first time, about six after that
knownIssues.cause: the game activates its packages and compiles its shaders before the start screen on every start; the engine keeps the compiled shaders, so later starts are shorter
knownIssues.fix: wait for the start screen; the loading screen shows its progress, and the first minute may stay blank before the first loading video

knownIssues.cause: Steam is offline, and the game signs in to its servers through Steam
knownIssues.fix: put Steam online and start the game again

knownIssues.symptom: Turning the view or taking off leaves smeared trails behind buildings and lights
knownIssues.cause: the game's motion blur, on in the Medium preset, smears each frame's movement, and at the frame rates a Mac reaches every frame moves three to four times as far as at 60 frames per second
knownIssues.fix: Settings, General, Graphics, Global Rendering Quality, Motion Blur set to Off, then Ctrl+Return to apply

knownIssues.symptom: A brief freeze just before the start screen on every start
knownIssues.cause: the last frames of the 4K loading video trip a GPU fault on the Mac as the video ends, and the engine resumes the device at once
knownIssues.fix: none needed, the start screen follows; a fix in the engine's next revision

knownIssues.symptom: In daylight, a faint dark wedge drifts across the sky for a few seconds at a time while parked
knownIssues.cause: a volumetric effect the Mac route draws wrong (not the clouds, the light shafts or the terrain shadows, which were each turned off to check)
knownIssues.fix: none yet; it goes once airborne and never shows at night

knownIssues.symptom: A short hitch every 30 to 40 seconds in flight
knownIssues.cause: work on the game's side under the translation layer, not shader compiles (the engine keeps those from the first start on)
knownIssues.fix: none yet; the upscaler setting above keeps the rest of the frames steady
